intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for Canva on Mac. You hold ⌥⌘, ask your question, and Lazur answers out loud. It can circle a control you ask about, but it never clicks for you. This page covers what it does in Canva, where people get stuck, and what to check before you rely on it.

Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud.
Lazur points at controls and guides you one click at a time. You do the clicking.
Hold fn to dictate, or ask Lazur to draft text that lands at the cursor.

blocks.text: If you want an AI assistant for Canva on Mac, you want help that sees the screen you are looking at. Lazur runs in the notch at the top of your Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask your question. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. You stay in control of the mouse.
What Lazur does inside Canva on Mac

Lazur does five jobs in Canva. Each job starts with a key you hold. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Most people start with explain and point. The other jobs come later, once the basics feel easy.

items: Explain: hold ⌥⌘ and ask what a panel, icon or setting does.
Point: ask where a tool is, and Lazur circles it with a label.
Guide: ask how to finish a task, and Lazur walks you through it step by step.
Draft: ask for a headline, caption or alt text, and Lazur types the draft at the cursor.
Dictate: hold fn, speak, and clean text lands at the cursor in any app.

blocks.text: Why Canva on Mac needs a helper

Canva is large, and its users are varied. Canva reported more than 265 million monthly active users at the end of 2025, up 20% year over year. It also reported more than 31 million paid users. Annual recurring revenue reached about $4 billion. G2 even wrote a full analysis on non-designers taking over Canva. Many of those users are not trained designers. The learning curve data below shows why that matters.

The pain points repeat across review sets. Kimola's consumer report drew on more than 3,700 feedback entries from the App Store, Google Play, Trustpilot and Capterra. Of those pain points, 37% were performance issues such as crashes, lag and slow loading. Another 26% were download and export problems. These numbers come from all platforms, not only Mac, so treat them as a pattern rather than a Mac score.

The learning curve is the second big complaint. Kimola found that 30% of users reported a learning curve and navigation difficulties in early use. Another 19% described a steep learning curve. Users also struggle to find templates, text editing buttons and timeline controls. Finding those controls is where a pointing assistant helps most.

G2's analysis adds a different angle. Among education users (385 reviews), 8.57% of complaints concerned restrictions in the free version. Among small business users (1,261 reviews), 7.45% said the free version is too limited, and 2.46% cited slow performance with large files. Among non-profit users (69 reviews), 5.80% of complaints concerned export and download issues. The non-profit sample is small, so read that figure as a hint.
Explain what is on screen

Start with a plain question, not a command. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what you are looking at. Lazur reads the screen and answers out loud. This works well when a panel is new to you, or when a label is unclear. You do not need the feature name. Describe the thing in plain words.

Here is a worked example. You open a layout and see a row of small icons above the page. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask, 'What do these icons above the page do?' Lazur looks at the row, names what it can read, and says what each part does. A small or cut-off label gives a weaker answer, so zoom in first. Then ask a follow-up about one icon only.
Point at a button and get guided step by step

Sometimes you know the goal but not the button. Ask Lazur where the button is. It draws a circle and a label around the control on your screen. You still click it yourself. That keeps your hand on every change, which matters when a design is client work.

Pointing and guiding answer different questions. Pointing asks, where is it? Guiding asks, how do I finish this? For guiding, Lazur gives one step, then waits for your click before it moves on. If you get stuck, ask again and describe what you see.
A worked example: a second size for one design

Say you have a finished post and need a second size for another channel. Ask: 'Walk me through making a second size for this design.' Lazur names the first control to find, circles it, and waits. You click. Lazur then gives the next step. You stay in control of each click, and you can stop at any point.
Draft text at the cursor and dictate with fn

Canva work is full of short text. Headlines, captions, alt text and button labels all need words. Hold fn to dictate. Clean, formatted text lands at the cursor, in any app. You can also ask Lazur to draft text from a brief. It types the draft where your cursor sits, so put the cursor in the right box first.

Three dictation helpers are worth setting up early. Snippets hold a block of text you reuse, such as a brand line or a standard credit. The personal dictionary holds names and product words that speech tools often misspell. Clipboard slots keep copied text ready to reuse. Set up the dictionary before a big project, not in the middle of one.

blocks.text: A caption draft for a post

Say you have a post in Canva and need a caption that sounds warm and plain. Click into the caption box. Hold ⌥⌘ and say: 'Draft a short caption for this photo. Warm, plain, no hashtags.' Lazur reads the screen and types a draft at the cursor. Read it out loud. Change any word that does not sound like you. Then keep it.
How to ask a question Lazur can answer well
Good questions have three parts. Name the area, state the goal, and ask for the size of the answer you want. A vague question gets a vague answer. A clear question gets a step you can use.

items: Name the area: 'In the left panel, what does this tab do?'
State the goal: 'I want this headline bigger. Where do I start?'
Ask for one step: 'Give me only the first step.'
Keep it to one idea. Two ideas in one hold make the answer harder to follow.

blocks.text: Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Canva

items: Asking without holding the key. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold ⌥⌘ or fn.
Expecting Lazur to click. It points and guides. You do the clicking.
Dictating with the cursor in the wrong place. Text lands wherever the cursor sits, so click into the box first.
Skipping the dictionary. Brand names and product words come out wrong until you add them.
Trusting a draft without reading it. Check names, facts and tone before you publish.
Waiting until the deadline to test exports. Export and download problems are common in review data, so test one file early.

blocks.title: Lazur does not click for you
blocks.text: Lazur points, explains and guides. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate Canva for you. Keep your hand on the mouse for every change.

blocks.title: What this page does not cover
blocks.text: Canva's help pages would not load while this page was researched. So this page does not list Canva keyboard shortcuts or menu paths. Ask Lazur to point at the control you need instead, since it works from what is on screen.
Edge cases worth knowing before you rely on it
Answers come out loud. In a shared studio or an open office, that can be awkward. Ask quieter questions, or wear headphones when you want privacy.

Small text is harder for any assistant to read. If a label is tiny, zoom Canva in before you ask. Also name what you mean in plain words. 'The box under the photo' works better than an internal name you do not know.
Lazur answers from what is on the screen in front of it. If the thing you need is off screen, scroll or move the window first. Then ask again.
Privacy: what gets sent and what stays on your Mac

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac.

This matters for client work. Many Canva files hold unreleased product shots, pricing or staff photos. Check your client agreement before you ask about those files out loud. Lazur's privacy rules do not replace your contract.
Mac setup and what to check first

Canva's download page says the Mac desktop app is for 'Macs with Intel and Apple chips.' It does not list a macOS version, a version number or a release date. Before you install, open Apple menu > About This Mac to check your chip and macOS version. Then compare them with the download page.

Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Start on the [download page](/download). The free trial needs no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) before you commit to a plan.
Research and everyday tasks while you design

Some tasks take longer than one question. Lazur can run research in its own Chrome tabs, using the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use this for a quick scan of public pages, such as a competitor's pricing page, and check the sources yourself.
Everyday tasks work by voice too. Ask Lazur to set a timer, add a reminder in Apple Reminders, or create a Calendar event. Put the export deadline in Reminders early, not on the morning it is due.
Where the marketer and social media guides fit

If you run campaigns, read [Canva for marketers on Mac](/for/marketers/canva). It covers resize, Brand Kits and review, step by step. Social media managers can read [Canva for social media managers on Mac](/for/social-media-managers/canva), which covers resize, scheduling and common fixes. Both pair well with the pointing and guiding steps above.
Start with one question

Pick one screen you already know. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what one control does. Then ask for one walkthrough on a small task, such as a second size or a caption draft. Lazur keeps a memory of your questions on your Mac, so your history is there when you return.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Canva on Mac without a plugin?
faq.answer: Yes, and no plugin is needed. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac, not a plugin or add-in for Canva. It works from what is on your screen. Lazur has no partnership with Canva.

faq.question: Can the AI assistant click buttons in Canva for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It points at the control, explains it, or guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on.

faq.question: What is the shortcut for asking about my screen?
faq.answer: Hold ⌥⌘, which is Option and Command, and ask your question. Lazur answers out loud. For dictation, hold fn and speak. Clean, formatted text lands at the cursor.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my designs all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Which macOS version do I need for Canva on Mac?
faq.answer: Canva's download page says 'Macs with Intel and Apple chips' and lists no macOS version. Check that page before you install. Compare it with the macOS version shown in Apple menu > About This Mac.

faq.question: Can Lazur draft text inside my Canva design?
faq.answer: Yes. Put your cursor in a text box, then ask Lazur for a draft. It types the draft where the cursor sits. Read it before you keep it, and change any names or facts that look wrong.
